To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The power of multimedia information-retrieval techniques can be balanced with the simplicity of interaction in interactive television, and (2) The simplicity and power of interactive television can be increased by providing multiple levels of sophistication in the interface, in increasing order, as a user repeatedly presses the same remote control button.

the design of a layered interface that accommodates varying degrees of sophistication in the interface is an important strategy for balancing the power of multimedia IR techniques and usability in interactive TV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a design methodology for interactive TV that balances the power of emerging MMIR tools with the simplicity of interface required for interactive TV.

the development of a design methodology that can be applied to the development of interactive TV applications that integrate emerging MMIR techniques, and that will ensure the resulting applications are usable and useful.
the design of a system that can support a wide range of users and usage scenarios, and we believe that our layered interface approach is an effective way to achieve this.
